title: Fine-Gray regression for the cumulative incidence of one cause
summary: The subdistribution hazard ratio: the effect of treatment on the cumulative incidence of one cause when a competing event can prevent it.

sizing._why: Sizing a Fine-Gray comparison needs the cumulative incidences of both causes and is a simulation; the log-rank form sizes a different quantity.

pinned_defaults: R: failcode = 1 and cencode = 0 named, although they are crr's defaults: data coding death as 1 would silently model death.
R: cov1 is a numeric MATRIX; crr takes no formula and does not expand factors.
_python_not_applicable: No standard Python package implements Fine-Gray regression. Writing one would mean replicating the censoring-weighted risk-set expansion, which is exactly the code that should come from a maintained implementation. The entry is R only; its recovery claim is checked by fitting 100 generated fixtures in R, and a second R implementation (survival::finegray with a weighted, clustered coxph) serves as the oracle.
_interpretation: The subdistribution hazard ratio is read through the cumulative incidence it implies, not as a rate among those at risk: its risk set keeps people who already had the competing event. For the rate of the event among those still event-free, see cause-specific-cox.
